elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "HDI shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence...".

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: "...and $2,000,000 in the aggregate" in the same CGL sentence.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $2,000,000".

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: "where HDI processes any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than $5,000,000" — the trigger captures every category of Customer data, not selected named types.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: "and workers' compensation insurance as required by law".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: "HDI shall provide certificates of insurance to the Company on request."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O set at not less than $2,000,000, which exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cyber and privacy liability set at not less than $5,000,000, exceeding the USD 2,000,000 fallback floor.

reasons: Finding classification 'missing' is corroborated: the cited General Provisions run through 10.8 (headings/counterparts) with no insurance obligation anywhere, and HDI hosts the Site and accesses Company Content, user information and data under Section 8.1.

All six preferred elements appear in a single inserted operative sentence pair with the correct amounts, bases (per occurrence vs aggregate), coverage lines, and party direction (HDI as the insuring party, Company as recipient of certificates).

The cyber trigger is drafted as 'any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company', which satisfies the requirement that the Customer Data trigger cover every category rather than selected named data types.

Minimality holds: the insertion omits model-language extras such as 'at its own expense' and the one-year survival tail, adds no procedures, audit rights or additional remedies, and no existing wording (including Section 10.8) was deleted, reworded or paraphrased.
Intent is preserved: nothing in the insertion contradicts retained allocation, indemnity, confidentiality or termination mechanics, and it introduces no undefined term or dangling cross-reference.

Drafting nit only (not a defect in an element): the inserted paragraph is rendered as 'Insurance.' without the Section 10.9 number referenced in the rationale and comment; number it 10.9 on execution for consistency with the numbering of 10.1-10.8.

Because the preferred checklist is fully met, the fallback (E&O $1M / cyber $2M) is exceeded on both lines and is correctly held back as a negotiation concession in the comment rather than drafted into the operative text.
